page: Amazon Web Services c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with symmetric multithreading enabled. The x86_64 CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, providing hardware instructions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and FMA. It is paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, and it provisions a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance sits in the middle 50 percent across Geekbench and stress-ng suites, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 6393.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13110.28. While cached small-block memory throughput reaches 567.48 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write speeds test in the bottom 25 percent at 38.9 GB/sec and 22.31 GB/sec respectively. Large language model inference remains viable for small 135M parameter models but degrades significantly on 7B models during prompt processing.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective allocation for compute-bound tasks that do not require extensive memory footprints. Workloads reliant on high uncached memory bandwidth or high local disk I/O face architectural tradeoffs due to DDR4 bus limitations and the lack of bundled local NVMe disks. Amazon Web Services c6a.2xlarge is technically appropriate for continuous integration builds, software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed compute worker nodes.
